column1: # Funcupdate / reassign elaborated-MIR golden baselines (#2648 interface pin, MIR half).
# generating-revision: 82a23b19b1a824a592c739a685c527d2c7efdab1
#   (rebased forward from 3683c2ac5; the closure/gen-fn string fixtures were
#   regenerated to carry the A240 string copy-on-write drop plan — string shares
#   are now Read/retain, so the source binding keeps a scope-exit drop and every
#   shared heap-string local drops via the cow_heap(hew_string_drop) destructor.
#   The two owned-record fixtures are byte-identical across both revisions.)
#   Refreshed for the caller-side by-value-param drop: owned by-value
#   record/tuple/enum params now carry a scope-exit `record_in_place` drop at
#   the caller. Only var_record_reassign_ownership_test.elab.mir shifted, and
#   purely additively — every hunk replaces a `(none)` scope-exit slot with a
#   `drop _N ty=<record/tuple> kind=record_in_place`, no CFG/terminator/value
#   change. The other three baselines remain byte-identical.
#   Refreshed for the fresh string-call/f-string temp-arg drop: a fresh
#   string produced by a string-returning call (or f-string) and passed to a
#   borrowing fn now carries a caller-side temp binding (`bind __hew_temp_arg
#   ty=string`) and its exactly-once scope-exit drop (`drop _N ty=string
#   kind=cow_heap(hew_string_drop)`), one drop per mutually-exclusive CFG exit
#   edge — no double-free. funcupdate_owned_field_drop_test.elab.mir and
#   var_record_reassign_ownership_test.elab.mir shifted purely additively
#   (paired temp-arg bind/drop plus `(none)` scope-exit slots becoming string
#   drops, no CFG/terminator/value change). The closure/gen-fn baselines remain
#   byte-identical.
#   Refreshed for the borrowing-callee temp-arg drop reaching Hew-BODIED
#   callees: `testing.assert_eq_str(c.label, string.repeat(...))` now carries the
#   same `bind __hew_temp_arg ty=string` / `drop _N ty=string
#   kind=cow_heap(hew_string_drop)` pair the string-call temp rule already gave
#   other borrowing callees. Only funcupdate_owned_field_drop_test.elab.mir
#   shifted, purely additively: three `(none)` scope-exit slots become string
#   drops, three paired bind/drop statements appear, and the only other changed
#   lines are the `eval site=SiteId(#N)` renumbering those binds push along. No
#   CFG, terminator or value change.
#   Why the NEW output is the correct one, measured rather than asserted:
#   `testing.assert_eq_str(actual: string, expected: string)` is Hew-BODIED
#   (std/testing/testing.hew), and `lower_params` registers both by-value
#   `string` parameters in `borrowed_string_param_locals` — the callee only
#   reads them and never releases them, so the caller holds the sole release
#   obligation for the fresh `string.repeat(...)` buffer it passes. The old
#   baseline recorded no such release, i.e. it froze a leak. A 200-iteration
#   loop of exactly this call shape, compiled at the previous
#   generating revision and run under `leaks --atExit` with MallocScribble,
#   MallocPreScribble and MallocGuardEdges, reports 200 leaked nodes / 12800
#   bytes — one per iteration. The same program compiled here reports 0 leaks
#   and exits cleanly under the same poisoned allocator, so the added drop is
#   exactly-once rather than a second release. The baseline was stale; the MIR
#   is right.
#   Refreshed for scanner-token call-carrier ownership at 82a23b19b: terminal
#   transferred/rebound record values now carry their `record_in_place` drops
#   on panic, cancel, and return edges. Only
#   funcupdate_owned_field_drop_test.elab.mir shifted, purely additively: 13
#   `(none)`/terminal slots gain the already-declared record owner drop; no CFG,
#   terminator, statement, value, or other fixture changes.
# dump-mode: hew compile --dump-mir elab <fixture>   (run from the repo root)
# normalization: two run-variance normalizations — (1) the dump's function
#   ORDER is nondeterministic (map iteration), so the harness splits both
#   sides into per-function chunks (column-0 `fn ` lines) and sorts by
#   signature line; (2) within each chunk, BindingId/SiteId values are
#   renumbered in first-occurrence order. Within-chunk content order is
#   preserved, so a reordered drop inside a chunk remains detectable.
# Purpose: the Coarse freshness summary (`compute_fn_returns_fresh_owner` /
# `return_value_may_alias_borrow`) feeds the destructive-funcupdate base gate
# (`expr_is_materialized_owner`) and the #2420 reassign-overwrite gate
# (`reassign_rhs_may_alias_binding`). The frozen-reference differential pins the
# boolean verdicts; THIS manifest pins the emitted elaborated MIR (including
# drop plans) of the fixtures that exercise those two consumers, so a Coarse
# drift that somehow escaped the boolean pin still fails here.
# Fixture universe (recorded justification, plan §Interface pin / manifest
# universe): the named fixtures below are the corpus inputs that exercise the
# funcupdate (`{ ..base, f }`) and var-reassign-overwrite consumers —
# funcupdate_owned_field_drop_test (funcupdate owner gate),
# var_record_reassign_ownership_test (#2420 reassign gate),
# closure_consume_reassign_overwrite_release and
# gen_fn_consume_reassign_overwrite_release (reassign gate inside closure / gen
# fn bodies). tests/corpus/v05-value-model/{03,18} also contain the surface
# syntax but do NOT compile at the generating revision (aspirational corpus:
# `..base` not last in field list), so they cannot reach either consumer and
# are excluded. A fixture that newly exercises these consumers must be added
# here WITH a regenerated baseline (an unmapped baseline file fails the test).
# Regeneration is an explicit, reviewed step only: rebuild `hew` at the wanted
# revision, re-run the dump-mode command per row, and record the new revision
# above. The harness (hew-cli/tests/funcupdate_mir_baselines.rs) never writes.
